summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze confidential supplier/ERP data, find where the launch plan hides shortfalls, and build a general recheck-and-act agent product (Lighthouse) with a polished UI before the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found the hidden Collector's Edition shortfalls (overbooked art book receipt, failed statue lot, packing speed) and built a poller, versioned store, pluggable LLM agent and approval UI. Late session added a 'How we got here' case flow and many UI fixes on main; main was still unpushed (about 17 commits ahead) at the 12:00 deadline.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored, only .env.example is committed.
The portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhooks. Files are replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 checksums by polling.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist in the repo; claim tasks in PROGRESS.md before coding.
The API does not load .env on import, so settings like ASK_VIEWER_TITLE must be read through a helper that loads .env first, otherwise they are missing after restart.

Routine steps are restricted by trigger kind: 'Chase once if no answer' works only on routines watching messages awaiting an answer, 'Ask for a status' only on shipment routines. The server rejects others with 'step N cannot be done on open decisions'.
Routines calls Claude (claude-opus-5-5) with the key from .env, independent of ASK_LLM_PROVIDER.
Case flow nodes reuse the exported connector and box from FlowGraph.tsx so the case flow and routine diagram share one drawing implementation.
Number keys 1-9 only choose an option; Cmd+Enter carries out the main button's action.
Parallel git worktrees (../ask-soony-pulse, ../ask-soony-flow) were used for branch work, each with preview servers on a copy of demo state (background off, email record-only).
workflow: Entire hooks log TurnStart/TurnEnd per session and skip checkpoints when no repo files changed; checkpoints appear only once a commit contains session changes.
Subagents handled bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations, 59 scans) and logo design in the background without touching the repo.
Verifying UI changes with headless-browser screenshots at desktop and phone widths caught layout problems like the right-to-left snake and top-bar crowding.
A feature merged to main was undone when the user said it misread their intent (a second chat instead of Pulse's flow view); keeping work on a branch made the revert cheap.
Interview notes in the repo's commits helped settle design direction (decision view over chat pipeline).

friction: Misread the team's request for Pulse's UI: built a duplicate 'Describe it' chat, merged it, then had to revert.
The two-column snake layout of the case flow read right-to-left and confused the user, requiring a rework to a single column.
Top bar crowding, phone bottom-bar overlap with options, and auto-scroll on phone load each needed separate fixes late in the session.
The user interrupted an edit; the Details toggle showed the full flow instead of compact, requiring a check of whether the partial edit had landed.
The 'Chase once if no answer' step silently failed because the menu offered it on incompatible routines.
The portal login password ended up in Discord history.
Time pressure: many UI polish requests landed in the final 20 minutes before the 12:00 hand-in.
open_items: main is about 17 commits ahead of origin and was not pushed for the hand-in; live also needs a restart to pick up the new server code.
Logo: four Lighthouse variants drawn (the subagent recommended 2, the assistant 3); none chosen or applied to the favicon, top bar or sign-in page.
Routines page is messy with many routines: planned compact list rows, a ⋯ menu, duplicate-routine detection and a clearer order, deferred until after the hand-in.
Decision routines cannot yet send an email and then chase once on no reply; a reply-watching follow-up is needed.
A phone bottom-sheet drawer for the case list was proposed for after the hand-in.
Lucas's 'read new documents before verifying' step has not been ported; the parked branch jonas/pulse-ui is not on main.
Briefing page and Claude docs still show the 14:00 state, not the 14:37 drop; the earlier Claude doc may be deleted.
Sender email addresses must be registered in the portal Settings, and the Karton Nowak art-book offer and Boise terms reply were never sent.
Open questions remain for the Lio engineers on whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
